title: Cryptographic Inventories and Risk Assessment
summary: How firms discover and record where and how cryptography is used, prioritise exposed systems and data, and how supervisors judge whether an inventory is complete and decision-useful.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How firms discover and record where and how cryptography is used, prioritise exposed systems and data, and how supervisors judge whether an inventory is complete and decision-useful.
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose and contents of a cryptographic inventory
Assess the completeness of a firm's inventory, including third-party and embedded uses
Evaluate a firm's prioritisation of systems by exposure and data shelf life
Syllabus: Discovery tools, manual review and the cryptographic bill of materials
Prioritising by data sensitivity, shelf life and system criticality
Governance: ownership, board reporting and risk appetite
Red flags: partial inventories and no named owner
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors responsible for technology, cyber and operational resilience risk
Payments, market infrastructure and digital asset specialists in supervisory and central bank functions
Policy staff and senior managers shaping the authority's cyber and quantum readiness approach
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of cyber, technology risk or operational resilience supervision is helpful. No background in mathematics or cryptography is required.
Core Reading: NIST, FIPS 203, 204 and 205: Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards (2024)
G7 Cyber Expert Group, Public Statement on Planning for the Opportunities and Risks of Quantum Computing (2024)
